sequence.implementation: ALSO WRONG - Both implemented immediately without verification

events.system_impact: ERROR: Parameter not found, downstream service fails

events.discovery: Parameter was removed but still used internally

events.system_impact: 23 undetected GC pauses cause data inconsistency
events.customer_impact: Audit compliance question - data drift detected by customer

events.severity: CRITICAL - Data integrity may be compromised

actions: Audit 72 hours of elections for drift

events.event: Recovery complete - parameter restored, monitoring active
events.status: RECOVERING - Back to pre-crisis state but damaged

events.event: Full investigation of what went wrong
findings: Implementation was too fast (no verification step)
Risk was NOT communicated to stakeholders

recovery.scenario: After both wrong decisions cascaded to incidents

framework_enabled_recovery.how: Framework had flagged both decisions as low-confidence
framework_enabled_recovery.timing: Should have triggered escalation at Day 0

framework_enabled_recovery.how: Framework ledger shows D1 REMOVE → D2 IGNORE anomaly monitoring
Framework shows decisions were contradicting recommendations
Follow original framework recommendations this time
framework_enabled_recovery.timing: Day 5+: Coherence recovers to 99.2% by following right path

gates.scenario: Same decisions (D1 REMOVE, D2 IGNORE) but framework enforces gates

execution.consequence_shown: Removing kills 3 internal queries (traces found by framework)

execution.test_result: Parameter removal fails 3 internal queries immediately
execution.team_can_do: Fix code, re-test, try again at Day 2

execution.NEW_OUTCOME: Incident happens at their desk, not customer's

strength_1.name: Ledger cannot be rewritten
strength_1.revelation: Even with cascade failure, history is preserved
strength_1.implication: Root cause analysis works perfectly on Day 7

strength_2.name: Wrong decisions leave trace
strength_2.revelation: Framework warned about D1 and D2 from the start
strength_2.implication: Future decisions can learn from this cascade

strength_3.name: Recovery is traceable
strength_3.revelation: Framework shows Day 5 recovery following original recommendation

strength_4.name: Organization can add gates without coercion
strength_4.revelation: 2-hour verification window catches D1 problem at desk, not production
strength_4.implication: Framework evolves based on post-incident analysis

phase_2_investigation.focus: Why did we ignore framework recommendations?

policy_updates: Rule 1: Decisions contradicting framework need executive approval
Rule 2: Implementation has 2-hour verification window before deployment
Rule 3: Anomaly monitoring is automatic, cannot be disabled without investigation

phase_4_framework_evolution.action: Framework upgrades to V2 with gates
phase_4_framework_evolution.prevention: Unlikely this cascade can happen again with new policy

insight.core_truth: Even catastrophic failures reveal that framework works
evidence: Cascade failure created incidents in 48 hours (fast enough to be detectable)
Framework ledger preserved all decisions and their consequences
Recovery followed original framework recommendation, succeeded
Root cause was traceable: 'We ignored warning signs'
insight.conclusion: Framework doesn't prevent bad decisions. It makes them: (1) VISIBLE via coherence metrics, (2) TRACEABLE via ledger, (3) REVERSIBLE via recovery procedures, (4) EDUCATIONAL via root cause analysis, (5) PREVENTABLE via policy evolution

conclusion: Even catastrophic failures prove framework works by enabling detection, traceability, recovery, and learning
